# Clarified executable specification

The required artifact is a regular executable file named `executable`. It is a terminal-oriented nonsense-activity generator compatible with the behavior below. All text is UTF-8. Unless a section says otherwise, normal output goes to stdout, diagnostic parse errors go to stderr, successful commands return 0, and parse errors return a nonzero status. Blocks introduced as exact output end with one newline and permit no extra stdout/stderr text.

## Spec 1

The command-line interface is named `executable` for usage/error rendering, while its product name is `genact`. It accepts:

- `-l`, `--list-modules`
- repeatable `-m MODULES`, `--modules MODULES`
- `-s SPEED_FACTOR`, `--speed-factor SPEED_FACTOR` (default `1`)
- `-i INSTANT_PRINT_LINES`, `--instant-print-lines INSTANT_PRINT_LINES` (default `0`)
- `--inhibit`
- `--exit-after-time EXIT_AFTER_TIME`
- `--exit-after-modules EXIT_AFTER_MODULES`
- `--print-completions SHELL`
- `--print-manpage`
- `-h`, `--help`
- `-V`, `--version`

The only accepted module names, in canonical order, are: `ansible`, `bootlog`, `botnet`, `bruteforce`, `cargo`, `cc`, `composer`, `cryptomining`, `docker_build`, `docker_image_rm`, `download`, `julia`, `kernel_compile`, `memdump`, `mkinitcpio`, `rkhunter`, `simcity`, `terraform`, `uv`, `weblog`, and `wpt`. A comma-separated value is one value and is not split. Repeating `--modules` is the way to supply several modules, and repeated identical values are legal and are not an error.

/bin/bash -lc "cat >> /workspace/eval/test_executable.py <<'EOF'

def test_download_terminal_progress():
    rc,out=terminal('-m','download','-s','50','--exit-after-modules','1',timeout=6); s=out
    completed=[x for x in s.splitlines() if '100%[================' in x]
    assert rc==0 and len(completed)>=2
    assert all(re.search(r'100%\\[=+\\].*(?:B/s|KiB/s|MiB/s).*eta [0-9]+s',x) for x in completed)
    assert any(re.search(r'\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?MiB/s',x) for x in completed); saved(s)

def test_docker_build_terminal_progress():
    rc,out=terminal('-m','docker_build','-s','10000','--exit-after-modules','1',timeout=10); s=out
    assert rc==0 and re.search(r'Step \\d+/\\d+',s) and ('Successfully built' in s or 'Successfully tagged' in s)
    saved(s)

def test_ansible_tasks_and_hosts():
    rc,out=terminal('-m','ansible','-s','100','--exit-after-modules','1',timeout=6); s=out
    assert rc==0 and len(re.findall(r'"'^TASK '"\\[\\w+ : .+\\] \\*{10,}"'$'"',s,re.M))>=1
    hosts=re.findall(r'"'^(?:ok|changed|failed|skipping): '"\\[([0-9a-fA-F:.]+)\\]',s,re.M)
    assert len(set(hosts))>=5 and len(re.findall(r'"'^ok: '"\\[',s,re.M))>=5
    assert re.search(r'"'^(?:changed|failed|skipping): '"\\[',s,re.M)

def test_bruteforce_time_limited_partial_output():
    rc,out=terminal('-m','bruteforce','-s','100','--exit-after-time','200ms',timeout=3); s=out
    assert rc==0 and '=> Hashes to decrypt' in s and '=> Extracting Rainbow Table' in s
    assert re.search(r'  [0-9a-f]{64}',s); saved(s)

def test_terraform_resources_have_provider_and_operations():
    rc,out=terminal('-m','terraform','-s','10000','--exit-after-modules','1',timeout=8); s=out
    assert rc==0 and s.startswith('Acquiring state lock.')
    types=re.findall(r'\\b(?:aws|azurerm|google)_[a-z0-9_]+\\.\\w+',s)
    assert len(set(types))>=5
    ops=['Creating...','Still creating...','Creation complete after','Modifying...','Still modifying...','Modifications complete after','Destroying...','Destruction complete after','Refreshing state...']
    assert sum(op in s for op in ops)>=2 and len(re.findall(r'(?:after \\d+s|\\[\\d+s elapsed\\])',s))>=2
    assert re.search(r'\\[id=\\w+\\]',s) and 'Apply complete"'!'"' not in s; saved(s)

item.text:
Created the test suite under `/workspace/eval` and made [`run.sh`](/workspace/eval/run.sh) executable. It runs the full pytest suite and writes JUnit XML to `/workspace/eval/results.xml`, including a fallback report if pytest fails to start.

The tests cover the documented CLI behavior and module outputs, including PTY-based modules. I did not run the suite.
